B-HTTP.name: HttpRetrieval
docs:
Expected HTTP behavior, including admission, cache freshness, source failure and client verification alternatives.
Guards are observed outcomes, not predictions made by this model.

B-HTTPS.name: HttpsRetrieval
docs:
Expected successful CONNECT/TLS exchange or admission denial. TCP/TLS failures stop
retrieval; retries and detailed transport error exchanges are outside this view.
Client-to-source messages pass through the established tunnel. No payload cache or scanning.

BOOT-DEF-operator.name: BootstrapOperator
docs: Person operating the bootstrap host.

CALC-shortcut.name: CacheShortcut
docs: Rejected candidate: a warm cache must not bypass admission. An analysis alternative, not an implementation.

DEF-cache.name: DisposableCache
docs:
Storage responsibility holding zero or more cached objects. Selected virtual disks
realize this part; the content remains a separate item feature.

DEF-cached-content.name: CachedContent
docs:
Stored response data and associated cache metadata. Disposable copies, not an executing
component, authoritative retention, or evidence of publisher trust.

DEF-client.name: UpdateClient
docs: Pull through the accepted route and verify publisher metadata/signatures locally.

DEF-member.name: ProxyMember
docs: A software/virtual-resource member. Its guest storage does not identify a physical drive or host.

DEF-proxy.name: PolicyProxy
docs:
Admit by client, destination and port before forwarding or cache lookup.
Reject disallowed requests without contacting the source or reading cached content.
Forward encrypted tunnels without payload inspection.
Cache eligible HTTP responses only; a cache hit conveys no release approval.

DEF-source.name: ApprovedSource
docs: Abstract role of an external repository service; an allowlist is a separate policy asset.

F-admit.name: Check request access
docs: Check the accepted client, destination and port policy before content access.

F-cache.name: Reuse fresh cached content
docs: Reuse only eligible fresh responses; respect privacy and freshness directives. Storage remains disposable.

F-http.name: Fetch content from source
docs: Fetch or conditionally revalidate permitted repository content with its source.

F-tunnel.name: Forward HTTPS traffic
docs: Establish an admitted tunnel; preserve client-to-source TLS without inspecting or caching encrypted payload.

F-verify.name: Verify before use
docs: The external client verifies trusted publisher metadata and signatures; failure stops use.

H-denied.name: Deny without a cache lookup or source fetch

L-Consumers.name: Update Consumers
docs: Separately owned external client roles; not a shared network or authority.

L-Sources.name: Approved external sources
docs:
Abstract external repository role, not a component implemented by this system.
The permitted-source list is admission policy/configuration, not this participant.

L-context.name: context
docs:
Interaction context. Tier and zone frames are explanatory view classifications,
not deployed parts or composition owners. External sources/clients are reference roles.

P-storage-network.name: Logical storage network
docs: Optional dual-fabric reference. Not required by the selected local cache disks.

REQ-custody.name: independentRecovery
docs: Losing rebuildable cache data must not erase the independently retained recovery supply.

REQ-egress.name: noBypass
docs: Independently enforce the accepted network egress policy. Proxy configuration alone cannot deny bypass.

REQ-integrity.name: consumerVerification
docs: Preserve source TLS through CONNECT and consumer verification. Cache presence is not approval.

REQ-policy.name: admittedSources
docs: Remote access requires the accepted client, destination and port policy; otherwise deny.

S-fetch.name: Fetch through client-to-source TLS
docs: Client authenticates source TLS through the tunnel. No payload caching or scanning.

S-verify.name: Verify trusted metadata / signatures; stop on failure

SAT-policy.name: policySatisfied
docs: Design assertion for the selected policy proxy; verification and site evidence are separate.

SC-http-cache-untrusted.name: Reject untrusted cached content
docs: An update client requests HTTP repository content.
A fresh eligible cached response is returned but publisher verification fails.
Reject cached content before use; a cache hit does not imply trust.

SC-http-denied.name: Reject a disallowed HTTP request
docs: A client requests a disallowed HTTP destination, port or route.
At least one admission condition fails.
Receive denial without a cache lookup or source fetch.

SC-http-hit.name: Reuse a fresh HTTP response
docs: An update client repeats an eligible HTTP request.
Policy admits the request and an eligible fresh cached response exists.
Receive cached content without an origin fetch, then perform the same local verification as a miss.

SC-http-miss.name: Retrieve or revalidate HTTP content
docs: An update client requests HTTP repository content.
The route and trust policy are configured; content is absent or needs revalidation.
Receive an allowed response, then verify trusted metadata and signatures locally. Verification failure stops use; it never approves an artifact.

SC-http-source-failure.name: Stop when the source is unavailable
docs: An update client requests HTTP repository content.
An admitted request has no eligible fresh response and its source attempt fails.
Return a retrieval error and stop without content verification.

SC-http-untrusted.name: Reject untrusted source content
docs: An update client requests HTTP repository content.
An admitted source retrieval completes but publisher verification fails.
Reject received content before use.

SC-https.name: Retrieve through source TLS
docs: An update client requests an HTTPS repository through CONNECT.
Admission succeeds; TCP and source-authenticated TLS can be established.

Receive content through the tunnel and verify it at the client. No TLS interception, payload caching or scanning. Transport or verification failure stops retrieval; detailed transport error exchanges are outside this sequence.

SC-https-denied.name: Reject a disallowed CONNECT request
docs: A client attempts a disallowed CONNECT request.
At least one admission condition fails.
Receive denial without a connection to the source.

SYS-delivery.name: Delivery and workloads
docs: Mapped boundary: reviewed source, builds, artifacts and scoped workload delivery.

SYS-operations.name: Operations and recovery
docs:
Mapped boundary: observation, protected evidence, maintenance and recovery.
Dependency on managed resources does not allocate independent recovery custody.

SYS-trust.name: Trust and access
docs:
Mapped boundary: cryptography, independent key custody and identity/access.
Offline custody is not implicitly hosted by the connected platform.

UC-clone.name: Clone a Git repository over HTTPS
docs: The operator starts git clone with an approved HTTPS repository URL on boot-1.

The accepted proxy is reachable, the Git source and CONNECT port are admitted,
the current shell uses the proxy, and TLS verification remains enabled.

1. The operator starts the clone on boot-1.
2. Git on boot-1 requests access through software intake.
3. Software intake admits the CONNECT request or returns a denial.
4. Git validates the source TLS certificate and exchanges repository data through the tunnel.
5. Git reports a local checkout or failure to the operator.

Software intake remains a supporting boundary here. Its internal design and HTTPS
exchanges have their own views. CONNECT payloads do not use the HTTP object cache.
Denial, source failure or TLS failure stops the clone; signed commit/tag approval is a
separate decision. This goal scenario is documented, not an executed Git verification case.

UC-clone-intake-behavior.name: Uses the accepted HTTPS access behavior

VC-custody.name: Demonstrate independent recovery
docs: Remove disposable cache data and demonstrate recovery from independently retained supply. This is a site recovery demonstration, not inferred from storage configuration.

VC-egress.name: Demonstrate bypass prevention
docs: Attempt direct external access bypassing the accepted route and show independent network enforcement rejects it. This requires the site network policy and deployed-route evidence.

VC-http-cache-untrusted.name: Reject untrusted cached content
docs: Cached content is verified at the client and rejected when trust fails, without a source fetch. Model trust is an input, not a cryptographic check.

VC-http-denied.name: Assess HTTP admission denial
docs: A rejected client, destination or port receives denial and the recording source sees no request.

VC-http-hit.name: Assess admitted cache reuse
docs: A repeated eligible fresh response is served without another origin request. The client still verifies trusted metadata/signatures.

VC-http-miss.name: Assess admitted HTTP retrieval
docs: An admitted miss or stale response reaches the source; cache/privacy rules are respected and the client verifies before use. Unsigned or expired metadata is rejected unless an explicit trusted-source exception was selected.

VC-http-source-failure.name: Return a retrieval error on source failure
docs: A source failure after an admitted miss produces no usable content, no client verification and no implicit stale fallback. The execution model supplies availability; deployed failure behavior needs separate evidence.

VC-http-untrusted.name: Reject untrusted retrieved content
docs: When publisher verification fails after retrieval, the client rejects the content before use. Model trust is an input, not a cryptographic check.

VC-https.name: Assess CONNECT admission
docs: An admitted CONNECT establishes source-authenticated client TLS. Encrypted payload is neither cached nor inspected; client verification still applies.

Run the Stage 1 accepted-source HTTPS retrieval on the deployed route; verify source certificate/hostname, payload integrity and refusal of invalid trust. The isolated HTTP fixture does not forward CONNECT.

VC-https-denied.name: Assess CONNECT denial
docs: A disallowed CONNECT destination, client or port receives denial without opening a source connection.

VC-integrity.name: Assess source and publisher trust
docs: Client authenticates the source TLS endpoint and rejects untrusted publisher metadata before use; test the selected trust exceptions explicitly. Successful CONNECT/TLS still needs site evidence.

X-HTTP.name: Retrieve
docs:
Executable HTTP refinement: one request, eligible fresh-cache reuse, one source attempt,
and client verification. Availability and trust are supplied environment outcomes.
No packet timing, retry, stale-if-error fallback, TLS or cryptographic execution.
